Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Santa Rosa and San Jacinto Mountains National Monument Rising abruptly from the desert floor, the Santa Rosa and San Jacinto Mountains National Monument reaches an elevation of 10,834 feet. Providing a picturesque backdrop to local communities, visitors can enjoy magnificent palm oases, snow-capped mountains, a national scenic trail, and wilderness areas. Its extensive backcountry can be accessed via trails from both the Coachella Valley and the alpine village of Idyllwild. Jointly managed by the BLM and the U.S. Forest Service, the Monument’s boundary encompasses about 280,000 acres, including public lands within the BLM’s California Desert Conservation Area and the San Jacinto Ranger District of the San Bernardino National Forest. The Monument includes two Federal wilderness areas -- the Santa Rosa and the San Jacinto. The Monument was established by an Act of Congress on October 24, 2000, "in order to preserve the nationally significant biological, cultural, recreational, geological, educational, and scientific values found in the Santa Rosa and San Jacinto Mountains" (Public Law 106-351). pages.text: Santander, Spain: A 2027 Guide to Its Waterfront Art Museums | National Geographic TRAVEL BEST OF THE WORLD Beloved by Spaniards, Santander Is Becoming a Global Art Mecca The easygoing beachfront city is getting a host of new and reborn museums. A 2014 transformation by landscape architect Fernando Caruncho more than doubled the size of Pereda Gardens, in the historic heart of Santander. Luis Fonseca, Getty Images By Eddi Fiegel Published October 20, 2026 Santander, a port city in northwestern Spain, has long seduced Spaniards with its spectacular horseshoe bay surrounded by rolling green hills and the Cantabrian mountains in the distance. But now the city, the capital of the Cantabria region, is poised to become an international art destination. In September 2026, the new arts, culture, and technology center Faro Santander opened in a historic building redesigned by acclaimed British architect David Chipperfield with a permanent collection including works by such legendary figures as el Greco, Rubens, Velázquez, and Goya. ( See all 25 of the destinations that made our list of the best places to visit in 2027. ) Meanwhile, 2027 will bring the first outpost of Madrid’s renowned Reina Sofía museum. The impressive Museum of Prehistory and Archaeology of Cantabria also has a new home designed by the Barcelona-based architecture practice Mendoza Partida. Art lovers are sure to appreciate the city’s walkable city center—where ornate, neoclassical façades sit alongside Baroque churches and grand, porticoed squares—and the wide sandy beaches lined with elegant fin-de-siècle villas.

pages.text: Saracens: Canada captain Sophie De Goede signs new Saracens deal - BBC Sport Image source, Shutterstock Published 18 November 2026 Former World Player of the Year Sophie De Goede has signed a new one-year deal with Saracens. The 27-year-old back-row forward has had three spells with Sarries since 2020 and played 44 times for the club, most recently helping them claim the Premiership Women's Rugby title with victory over Trailfinders in June to make it a league and cup double. The World Rugby Player of the Year and member of World Rugby's Dream XV in 2025-26 captained Canada to the World Cup Final where they lost to England at Twickenham in 2025. "This club has been instrumental in supporting my development over my entire professional career to date. I feel very lucky to have the chance to echo Saracens' loyally to me back to the club," De Goede told the club website. , external Director of Rugby Alex Austerberry added: "Securing the long term-services of the 25-26 World Rugby Player of the Year is huge for the club and illustrates the desire of the club to remain at the forefront of the women's game. "Since returning from injury, which saw her miss the entirety of the 2024-25 season, Sophie's game has hit new heights both on the international stage and in club colours. "Sophie played a significant role in the historic league and couple double and we are excited to see her game continue to evolve and develop as she drives Saracens forward for many years to come." Taylor employed a bold color palette and organized her designs to highlight the interaction of one color with another. She created her appliqué quilts block by block, often sewing the blocks to strips of pieced fabric. For this quilt she traced her left hand on a sheet of brown paper, which she then used as a pattern, cutting the shapes from old dresses. Taylor later produced other versions of this quilt, one of which was commissioned for the 1985 film The Color Purple . Yes No, don't ask again ✕ Close Sarawak: Defending Indigenous Land from The Bulldozers Print Donate Now On paper, the land around the Indigenous Rumah Jeffery community was covered by company concessions. For the Iban families who live there, it was home. Rumah Jeffery is in the Malaysian state of Sarawak, on the island of Borneo, the third largest in the world. The community grows food on the land, harvests forest products, fishes in nearby streams, maintains burial grounds, and protects sacred sites. Its cultural and spiritual relationship to the forest spans generations. When the timber company Zedtee began logging in the community’s ancestral territory without its consent in 2022, residents tried to stop the damage. They protested and asked the authorities to recognize their customary land. Instead, the Sarawak Forest Department issued an eviction notice, giving residents 30 days to dismantle their longhouse and leave. It would have meant losing land, livelihoods, forest resources, cultural identity, and community life. pages.text: Sarina Wiegman contract: Why England manager faces biggest challenge yet - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Sarina Wiegman has won the past three Women's European Championships - with the Netherlands in 2017 and England in 2022 and 2025 By Joe Bradshaw BBC Sport senior journalist Published 19 October 2026 When Sarina Wiegman took the reins as England manager in September 2021, she declared she had "come to bring the next level". Winner of the 2017 Women's Euros with her own Netherlands and runner-up at the subsequent World Cup in 2019, she certainly had the pedigree, but could she deliver on her promises? Five years on, Wiegman has pocketed two more European Championships and acquired another silver medal on the global stage. Not only that, but the success of her Lionesses exploded the women's game in this country, taking it not just to a new level, but to previously unthinkable heights. And yet on the day Wiegman extends her deal until after the Euros in 2029, her newest challenge could be her hardest yet. England manager Wiegman signs contract extension Published 19 October Why must England evolve? Wiegman's successful England teams have been built on a core group of players from an outstanding generation - but a few cracks have appeared this year. Seven of the team that started against world champions Spain in June also played in the Euro 2022 final against Germany - and their 4-0 defeat in Mallorca laid bare the gap England must bridge to the world's best. That result also consigned England to two rounds of play-offs to reach next summer's World Cup.

Savepoints SAVEPOINTs are a method of creating transactions, similar to BEGIN and COMMIT , except that the SAVEPOINT and RELEASE commands are named and may be nested. The SAVEPOINT command starts a new transaction with a name. The transaction names need not be unique. A SAVEPOINT can be started either within or outside of a BEGIN ... COMMIT . When a SAVEPOINT is the outer-most savepoint and it is not within a BEGIN ... COMMIT then the behavior is the same as BEGIN DEFERRED TRANSACTION. The ROLLBACK TO command reverts the state of the database back to what it was just after the corresponding SAVEPOINT. Note that unlike that plain ROLLBACK command (without the TO keyword) the ROLLBACK TO command does not cancel the transaction. Instead of cancelling the transaction, the ROLLBACK TO command restarts the transaction again at the beginning. All intervening SAVEPOINTs are canceled, however. The RELEASE command is like a COMMIT for a SAVEPOINT. The RELEASE command causes all savepoints back to and including the most recent savepoint with a matching name to be removed from the transaction stack. The RELEASE of an inner transaction does not cause any changes to be written to the database file; it merely removes savepoints from the transaction stack such that it is no longer possible to ROLLBACK TO

pages.text: Saving What’s Ours: The Data Rescue Project and the Fight for Public Data – Open Source Initiative Saving What’s Ours: The Data Rescue Project and the Fight for Public Data Part of the Deep Dive: Data Governance Webinar Series The Data Rescue Project (DRP) emerged as a collaborative effort to protect and preserve public datasets that are at risk of being lost, altered, or rendered inaccessible. Our work is based on the belief that public data belongs to the people and that preserving it is a civic responsibility. In this presentation, we reflect on how current threats to public data access expose weaknesses in the systems we rely on to ensure long-term access and stewardship. Our approach is not only technical; it is deeply community-driven. The Data Rescue Project brings together librarians, archivists, technologists, data stewards, and researchers from across disciplines. We recognize that no single organization or agency can solve the systemic problems of public data infrastructure alone. In moments of urgency, grassroots efforts can illuminate what larger institutions often miss: that data preservation is not only about files and formats, but about relationships, trust, and collective responsibility. This talk will highlight coordination among members of the DRP and our partners, including efforts to amplify active preservation work being done by groups like the Environmental Data and Governance Initiative (EDGI) and data repositories such as ICPSR’s DataLumos. View on TensorFlow.org Run in Google Colab View source on GitHub Download notebook Overview This notebook shows how to compress a model using TensorFlow Compression . In the example below, we compress the weights of an MNIST classifier to a much smaller size than their floating point representation, while retaining classification accuracy. This is done by a two step process, based on the paper Scalable Model Compression by Entropy Penalized Reparameterization : Training a "compressible" model with an explicit entropy penalty during training, which encourages compressibility of the model parameters. The weight on this penalty, \(\lambda\), enables continuously controlling the trade-off between the compressed model size and its accuracy. Encoding the compressible model into a compressed model using a coding scheme that is matched with the penalty, meaning that the penalty is a good predictor for model size. This ensures that the method doesn't require multiple iterations of training, compressing, and re-training the model for fine-tuning. This method is strictly concerned with compressed model size, not with computational complexity. It can be combined with a technique like model pruning to reduce size and complexity. In the field of NLP, language models have gone from hundreds of millions of parameters (BERT) to hundreds of billions of parameters (GPT-3) demonstrating significant improvements on downstream tasks. The scaling laws for large scale language models have also been studied extensively in the industry. A similar trend can be observed in the vision field, with the community moving to transformer based models (like Vision Transformer , Masked Auto Encoders ) as well. pages.text: sched — Event scheduler — Python 3.16.0a2 documentation Navigation index modules | next | previous | Python » 3.16.0a2 documentation » The Python standard library » Concurrent Execution » sched — Event scheduler | Theme Auto Light Dark | sched — Event scheduler ¶ Source code: Lib/sched.py The sched module defines a class which implements a general purpose event scheduler: class sched. scheduler ( timefunc = time.monotonic , delayfunc = time.sleep ) ¶ The scheduler class defines a generic interface to scheduling events. It needs two functions to actually deal with the “outside world” — timefunc should be callable without arguments, and return a number (the “time”, in any units whatsoever). The delayfunc function should be callable with one argument, compatible with the output of timefunc , and should delay that many time units. delayfunc will also be called with the argument 0 after each event is run to allow other threads an opportunity to run in multi-threaded applications. Changed in version 3.3: timefunc and delayfunc parameters are optional. Changed in version 3.3: scheduler class can be safely used in multi-threaded environments.
